senses.definition: Of shape:
senses.example: We sat at a round table to make conversation easier.

senses.definition: Complete, whole, not lacking.
senses.example: The baker sold us a round dozen.

senses.definition: Convenient for rounding other numbers to; for example, ending in a zero.
senses.example: One hundred is a nice round number.

senses.definition: Pronounced with the lips drawn together; rounded.
senses.example: "Supposing somebody sees you, with all those flowers too? Supposing somebody writes him a letter? Ooooh!" (a pure round open Tamil O.)

senses.definition: Outspoken; plain and direct; unreserved; not mincing words.
senses.example: a round answer

senses.definition: Finished; polished; not defective or abrupt; said of authors or their writing style.
senses.example: In his satires Horace is quick, round, and[…]pleasant.

senses.definition: Consistent; fair; just; applied to conduct.
senses.example: Round dealing is the honour of man's nature.

senses.definition: Large in magnitude.
senses.example: I have a good banker in this city, but I would not wish to draw upon the house until the time when I shall draw for a round sum.

senses.definition: Well-written and well-characterized; complex and reminiscent of a real person.
Vaulted.
Returning to its starting point.
senses.example: round trip, round journey, round walk

senses.definition: A circular or spherical object or part of an object.
senses.example: in labyrinth of many a round self-rolled

senses.definition: A circular or repetitious route.
senses.example: hospital rounds

senses.definition: A general outburst from a group of people at an event.
senses.example: The candidate got a round of applause after every sentence or two.

senses.definition: A song that is sung by groups of people with each subset of people starting at a different time.
A serving of something; a portion of something to each person in a group.
senses.example: They brought us a round of drinks about every thirty minutes.

senses.definition: A single individual portion or dose of medicine.
senses.example: Daniel underwent one round of chemotherapy in February but stopped after that single treatment, citing religious beliefs.

senses.definition: One slice of bread.
senses.example: For breakfast I had two rounds of toast and a mug of tea.

senses.definition: One sandwich (two full slices of bread with filling).
A long-bristled, circular-headed paintbrush used in oil and acrylic painting.
A firearm cartridge, bullet, or any individual ammunition projectile. Originally referring to the spherical projectile ball of a smoothbore firearm. Compare round shot and solid shot.
One of the specified pre-determined segments of the total time of a sport event, such as a boxing or wrestling match, during which contestants compete before being signaled to stop.
senses.example: And though Fightville, an MMA documentary from the directors of the fine Iraq War doc Gunner Palace, presents it more than fairly, the sight of a makeshift ring getting constructed on a Louisiana rodeo ground does little to shake the label. Nor do the shots of ringside assistants with spray bottles and rags, mopping up the blood between rounds

senses.definition: A stage, level, set of events in a game
senses.example: qualifying rounds of the championship

senses.definition: A rounded relief or cut at an edge, especially an outside edge, added for a finished appearance and to soften sharp edges.
A strip of material with a circular face that covers an edge, gap, or crevice for decorative, sanitary, or security purposes.
senses.example: All furniture in the nursery had rounds on the edges and in the crevices.

senses.definition: The hindquarters of a bovine; a round of beef.
A rung, as of a ladder.
senses.example: All the rounds like Jacob's ladder rise.

senses.definition: A crosspiece that joins and braces the legs of a chair.
A series of changes or events ending where it began; a series of like events recurring in continuance; a cycle; a periodical revolution.
senses.example: the round of the seasons    a round of pleasures

senses.definition: A course of action or conduct performed by a number of persons in turn, or one after another, as if seated in a circle.
senses.example: Women to cards may be compar'd: we play ¶ A round or two; when us'd, we throw away.

senses.definition: A series of duties or tasks which must be performed in turn, and then repeated.
senses.example:
The trivial round, the common task,
 Would furnish all we ought to ask; […]

senses.definition: A circular dance.
senses.example:
Come, knit hands, and beat the ground,
 In a light fantastic round.

senses.definition: Rotation, as in office; succession.
senses.example:
A Cave[…],
Where light and darkness in perpetual round
Lodge and dislodge by turns.

senses.definition: A general discharge of firearms by a body of troops in which each soldier fires once.
An assembly; a group; a circle.
senses.example: a round of politicians

senses.definition: A brewer's vessel in which the fermentation is concluded, the yeast escaping through the bunghole.
A vessel filled, as for drinking.
A round-top.
Alternative form of around.
senses.example: I look round the room quickly to make sure it's neat.

senses.definition: Alternative form of around.
senses.example: The invitations were sent round accordingly.

senses.definition: To shape something into a curve.
senses.example: The carpenter rounded the edges of the table.

senses.definition: To become shaped into a curve.
senses.example: The girl's figure, he perceived, was admirably proportioned; she was evidently at the period when the angles of childhood were rounding into the promising curves of adolescence.

senses.definition: To finish; to complete; to fill out; see also round out.
senses.example: She rounded out her education with only a single mathematics class.

senses.definition: To approximate (a number, especially a decimal number) by the closest whole number, or some other close number, especially a whole number of hundreds, thousands, etc.; see also round down, round up.
senses.example: The exact amount was $101.65, but we rounded it to $100.

senses.definition: To turn past a boundary.
senses.example: Helen watched him until he rounded the corner.

senses.definition: To turn and attack someone or something (used with on).
senses.example: As a group of policemen went past him, one of them rounded on him, grabbing him by the arm.

senses.definition: To advance to home plate.
senses.example: And the runners round the bases on the double by Jones.

senses.definition: To go round, pass, go past.
senses.example: Diouf rounded Zaluska near the byeline and crossed but Daniel Majstorovic headed away and Celtic eventually mopped up the danger.

senses.definition: To encircle; to encompass.
senses.example:
The inclusive verge
 Of golden metal that must round my brow.

senses.definition: To grow round or full; hence, to attain to fullness, completeness, or perfection.
senses.example: The queen your mother rounds apace.

senses.definition: To do ward rounds.
To go round, as a guard; to make the rounds.
senses.example: They […] nightly rounding walk.

senses.definition: To go or turn round; to wheel about.
To speak in a low tone; whisper; speak secretly; take counsel.
To address or speak to in a whisper, utter in a whisper.
senses.example: rounded in the ear

senses.definition: A whisper; whispering.
Discourse; song.
A surname.

wordFamily: square peg in a round hole
let the grass grow round one's feet
